name: Macro-based loop unrolling (Extreme C example 1.6)
listed_description: Variadic preprocessor macro expands a loop into straight-line repeated statements instead of a real C loop, trading binary size for speed in embedded and constrained environments.
claim_text: Qualitative only: unrolled straight-line instructions avoid looping overhead and give better performance at the cost of larger binary size. No numbers given.
book_benchmark: None. The book shows the preprocessed output of ExtremeC_examples_chapter1_6.c but never times it against a normal for or while loop.
guessed_baseline: plain for/while loop compiled with gcc or clang -O2 (compilers already unroll)
found_in: book: Extreme C (2019), ch. 1 Essential Features, sections Variadic macros and Advantages and disadvantages of macros
